about.title: Morro Bay Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Morro Bay's small size means many residents rely on a handful of local clinics, urgent care centers, or a short drive into San Luis Obispo for hospital-level care. When a provider misreads test results, delays a referral, or makes a surgical error, the harm can be serious and the questions overwhelming. California treats medical malpractice differently than a typical injury claim — MICRA sets specific notice periods, filing deadlines, and rules around expert testimony that make these cases harder to pursue without guidance. LawProactive doesn't practice law or represent you directly; we simply connect Morro Bay residents with an independent attorney experienced in evaluating whether a bad medical outcome may have crossed into negligence. There's no cost to ask, and no fee unless the attorney recovers compensation on your behalf. A poor result doesn't automatically mean malpractice occurred, which is exactly why an informed review matters.

items.title: Strict, Layered Deadlines
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider. Missing any part of this sequence can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped — But the Cap Rises
items.desc: MICRA places a statutory limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, and that cap increases annually. An attorney familiar with the current-year figure can help you understand what's realistically at stake.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California law generally requires a qualified medical expert to support a malpractice claim, since a bad outcome alone doesn't prove negligence. Independent attorneys in our network work with the right medical experts to evaluate whether the standard of care was actually breached.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after treatment in Morro Bay — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor result by itself doesn't establish negligence. An independent attorney would need to review your records alongside a qualified medical expert to determine whether the care fell below the accepted standard. That's the kind of review LawProactive can help you access at no cost.

items.question: How much time do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but never more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a mandatory 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed, so acting sooner rather than later matters. An attorney can confirm exact dates based on your specific facts.

items.question: Does Morro Bay's small size affect how these cases are handled?
items.answer: Not in terms of the law itself — MICRA and California's malpractice rules apply the same way regardless of city size. It can mean your care involved a local clinic before a referral or transfer to a larger San Luis Obispo County facility, which is a detail an attorney will want to understand when reviewing your treatment timeline.
